thread.title: Wild times: The NHL team announced its games will be streamed on Prime Video
thread.title_full: Wild times: The NHL team announced its games will be streamed on Prime Video

author: Judd Zulgad
title: Wild times: The NHL team announced its games will be streamed on Prime Video
text:
There was a time when sports fans dreamed of the day they would be afforded the opportunity to watch their favorite teams in an a la carte format. That way they wouldn’t be stuck with hefty cable and satellite bills to pay for programming they didn’t want.
So why are so many sports enthusiasts upset that that day has arrived? Because it’s nothing like they imagined.
The original thought was that Regional Sports Networks (RSN) — such as Fox Sports North turned Bally Sports turned FanDuel Sports Network — would be made available in a package that only featured sports networks.
The problem is what no one saw coming was the implosion of the RSN model. That left teams and leagues without a vital revenue source and forced them to go it alone. Instead of being able to watch the Lynx, Timberwolves, Twins and Wild all on one channel, fans not only have to pay to watch each one, but they also must figure out where games are being shown.
This includes big national television contracts — the NBA is entering the second season of an 11-year, $76 billion broadcasting agreement — that makes multiple subscriptions necessary to watch your favorite teams on a nightly basis.
“Fans used to be able to get all of their favorite teams’ games in one spot,” said Mitch Helgerson, the Wild’s chief revenue officer and executive vice president. “That is no longer the case, and that’s the downside of this. If we all had the ideal scenario, we would still be able to do that. But the world has changed.”
WILD PARTNERS WITH PRIME VIDEO
The Wild revealed their plans to start their own network in July.
On Wednesday, the team announced it had entered into a multiyear local streaming agreement with Prime Video to show all of its non-nationally televised games and first-round playoff games. Fans can watch games on Prime by paying $19.99 a month or $99.99 for an annual subscription. The NHL also was involved in an agreement that placed five other teams — Anaheim, Carolina, Columbus, Dallas and St. Louis — under the Prime umbrella.
The subscription is available to all Amazon customers, meaning you don’t have to be a Prime member to stream games. However, Prime members will have to pay the subscription price to watch games on what will be branded as Wild+.
If you were used to watching the Wild on cable or satellite, there will be channels dedicated to carrying their games. (No word yet on if YouTube TV will be involved.) That’s the same setup Major League Baseball has used in helping several teams, including the Twins, air games in recent years. The Twins channel doesn’t carry programming until a brief pregame show comes on and is followed by the game.
To watch Twins.TV via streaming, it costs the same monthly and yearly prices that the Wild will charge. The Twins also have a package of 10 games that aired free this season on FOX9. The Wild are expected to have an over-the-air partner show a yet-to-be disclosed number of games. Last season, KSTC (Ch. 45) carried four Wild games and sister-station KSTP (Ch. 5) had one. It’s likely the Wild will return to one or both of those channels.
The Wild also will have 17 games aired exclusively on national television. That includes two on ABC, five on ESPN, three on ESPN+/Disney+/Hulu and seven on TNT.
THE WOLVES’ PLAN
The Timberwolves have yet to announce a price for what it will cost to watch their games via the DAZN streaming service. DAZN will broadcast 15 local games for free on its app without requiring a paid subscription, and there is expected to be a package of games shown on over-the-air television.
But, unlike with the Wild and Twins, there will be no cable and satellite arrangement, so you will have to subscribe to DAZN to watch the majority of Wolves games. The Wolves’ star appeal — with Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball leading the way — means they won’t be lacking for national coverage either.
